history.text: Lost world title recognition when the WWWF rejoined the NWA and was treated as a regional title.
Regained world championship status after the WWF conclusively left the NWA.
WWF bought WCW, acquiring its championship.
Unified at Vengeance; the WWF title kept its lineage and the WCW title was retired.
Brand split: title made exclusive to SmackDown while a separate world title was created for Raw.
Dropped the "undisputed" name and became exclusive to SmackDown.
Briefly became an ECW brand title after Rob Van Dam won it at ECW One Night Stand.
Reactivated and awarded to Van Dam, who held both titles.
ECW brand disbanded, deactivating the ECW Championship.
Rey Mysterio won the vacated title, then lost it to John Cena the same night.
First brand split ended; the title could appear on both Raw and SmackDown.
Orton beat Cena at TLC, unifying the titles; the World Heavyweight Championship was retired.
Brand split reintroduced; the title was moved to SmackDown in the 2016 WWE Draft.
Universal Championship created for Raw, leaving the WWE title exclusive to SmackDown.
Champion Brock Lesnar quit SmackDown and moved the title to Raw.
Roman Reigns beat Lesnar at WrestleMania 38 to hold both titles, defended jointly as the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship.
Reigns drafted to SmackDown, making the title exclusive to SmackDown.
Universal Championship deactivated; the WWE title continued as the Undisputed WWE Championship.
Universal Championship lineage retired after WrestleMania 41, with Reigns as its final champion.
